findings.charge: EV-3 carries the live member 'successive-call expiry/revocation' verbatim, then specifies only the revocation limb. The expiry limb has no exactByteIntent and no passProperty anywhere in the artifact.
evidence: EV-3 measures re-scopes the member to 'File 03's four revocation positions, including between successive broker calls.' — revocation only.
EV-3 exactByteIntent enumerates FX-5's four revocation positions plus FX-8's two halves — revocation only.
EV-3 passProperty reads 'Each FX-5 position yields the deterministic raceSemantics outcome. FX-8 is INVALID if only the brokered half is run.' — revocation only. suppliedBy is 'FX-5, FX-8.'

permission-truth-tables.v9 raceSemantics R-10 is 'An EXPIRY falling between acceptance and commit-intent', a race distinct from all four FX-5 revocation positions. Its outcome: 'Expiry is materialized as a journaled record at the sequence where the host observes it ... It is NOT evaluated by comparing a wall-clock expiry timestamp against a wall-clock now at commit time; doing so would make the clock the order, which DR-G09 forbids.' whyDeterministic: 'The expiry RECORD, not the expiry TIME, is what other records are ordered against.'
R-10 and FX-7 are the only two places in v9 that name DR-G09's forbidden-ordering rule as a requirement. The subject carries FX-7 and drops R-10.

No FX class supplies R-10. v9 FX-5's intent is scoped to 'File 03's own four conformance positions', so FX-7 — defined as re-running FX-4 and FX-5 under clock perturbation — never exercises an expiry either.
FX-13 does not rescue it: v9 FX-13 binds an 'expiry' field but asserts 'presence and binding structure only', which the subject itself repeats in EV-1.
findings.whyThisIsNotPedantry: The failure mode DR-G09's waiver rule exists to catch is a host that decides expiry by comparing a wall-clock timestamp to wall-clock now. A harness built exactly to this specification retains zero bytes that would distinguish that host from a conforming one, while the register row would report 'successive-call expiry/revocation' as retained evidence. That is a false-pass path on the member's own text.
findings.refutationAttempted: Read 'successive-call expiry/revocation' as a compound where expiry needs no separate evidence because v9 says expiry 'behaves exactly as REV from that point'. This fails: the equivalence to REV begins only AFTER materialization, and materialization is the whole testable content of R-10 — a REV record arrives from an actor, whereas an expiry must be manufactured by the host from a time value. The clause the subject would rely on for coverage is precisely the clause that makes the uncovered step the only one that matters.
findings.aggravating: The artifact demonstrates elsewhere that it knows how to disclose a ride — EV-1 states 'Identity VALUES for Run/operation ride DR-006; this member asserts presence and binding structure only.' No comparable disclosure is made for expiry. The narrowing is silent.
findings.whatWouldLandIt: Either give the expiry limb its own exactByteIntent and passProperty (expiry materialized as a journaled record at the observing sequence; no wall-clock expiry-vs-now comparison at commit; PR-5 thereafter), or state explicitly, in the artifact, that the expiry limb rides a named elsewhere and is not retained at G09.

findings.charge: EV-4's pass predicate 'Cleanup closes within its declared bound' does not name the bound's origin, and the artifact gives no exact-byte intent for process death — the one race named in the matrix string the subject carries as its own scope that no member specifies.
evidence: The subject's matrix, carried verbatim from the live harness cell, ends 'races at request acceptance, reversible commit, irreversible effect-commit, revocation, and process death'. Mapping the five: request acceptance and reversible commit and irreversible effect-commit and revocation are all specified in EV-3/EV-5/EV-6. Process death is specified nowhere.

v9 raceSemantics R-6 is 'PROCESS DEATH mid-cleanup', outcome: 'Recovery re-runs cleanup from the journal. Every inverse is idempotent by its effect class's own declaration, so re-running is safe by construction. Cleanup's bound is measured from the recovery, and exhausting it journals a residual rather than looping.'

EV-4 measures reads 'Cleanup closes within its declared bound; duplicate/concurrent revocations do not restart or extend it.' That is R-5. EV-4 exactByteIntent covers duplicate and concurrent revocations, CLN written exactly once, and bound-exhaustion journaled as a residual. Neither states that after a process death the bound is re-measured FROM RECOVERY, nor that cleanup re-runs, nor that inverse idempotence is what makes re-running safe.

The two rules sit in tension as written: R-5 forbids restarting or extending the bound, R-6 re-measures it from recovery. EV-4 states the first and is silent on the second, so its single pass predicate is evaluated differently depending on which origin an implementer assumes.
findings.whyThisIsNotPedantry: A host that abandons cleanup after a mid-cleanup process death passes EV-4 exactly as written, because EV-4 only delivers duplicate and concurrent revocations — it never kills the process. EV-2's FX-4 does not cover it either: every FX-4 assertion the subject carries ('no duplicate sequence number; no gap filled by renumbering; no *-INTENT without a terminal outcome or recorded INDETERMINATE; no effect initiated whose intent record is absent') is a journal-ordering assertion, all of which hold on a host that leaves cleanup unfinished. The member 'cancellation/cleanup closure' would then be reported as retained while cleanup demonstrably did not close.
findings.refutationAttempted: Argue R-6 is discharged by construction, since v9 says idempotence 'is a precondition of an effect class being called reversible at all ... so this case needs no special reasoning'. This softens the case for owing a fixture but does not answer the charge: v9 says the REASONING needs no special case, not that the EVIDENCE is owed elsewhere, and a harness specification's product is retained bytes, not design claims. Independently of whether a fixture is owed, EV-4's pass predicate is under-determined on the bound's origin, and the subject nowhere states that process death is discharged by construction — it is simply absent.
findings.whatWouldLandIt: Name the bound's origin in EV-4's pass property for both cases (from r under duplicate/concurrent revocation; from recovery after process death), and either give process death exact-byte intent under EV-4 or state in the artifact that R-6 is discharged by construction and retains no bytes at G09.

verdictStatement: REJECT at 2 blockers and 1 SHOULD-FIX. The artifact's provenance is clean and its refusals are sound: every cited digest matches, every verbatim carry is exact, the fourteen FX classes are held unauthored, FX-2B is held to DISCLOSURE, FX-8 is held to both halves, EE-6b is held to honesty, the G09 owner is not collapsed, required-now is unmoved, and closure of OBL-G09-HARNESS-SPEC is conditioned on ACCEPT and recording rather than on this file existing. It fails on coverage. EV-3 carries a compound member and specifies half of it, leaving the expiry materialization rule — the one race v9 ties by name to DR-G09's own forbidden-ordering waiver — with no retained bytes. EV-4 states a bound without an origin and leaves process death, a race named in the matrix the subject carries as its own scope, unspecified. Both gaps are silent: the artifact discloses rides elsewhere and does not disclose these. A harness specification whose product is exact-byte intent for six named members cannot ship with one member half-specified and another under-determined against a race it claims.
